title: EDGE: DCGain wrong finite value / wrong Inf next to near-DC or exact DC poles
body:
Found in wave 12 (fix/wave12). DCGain disagrees with FreqResponse(0) and the exact rational oracle when the DC solve is near-singular: absolute coefficient floors drop tiny B, transfer-limit path returns neither Inf nor the exact value, MIMO near-DC poles, and an exactly singular dense block missed by dcGainByBlockLaurent. All pre-existing on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #16 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value at a reachable, observable continuous integrator (MATLAB gives Inf). Repro: sys := &System{A: [[0,0],[1,-1.3258457598967608e-08]], B: [7.29653485561532e-14; 1.0337733234010072e-13], C: [0 1], D: [0]} (continuous). DCGain gives 7.797085843999098e-06/nil; FreqResponse(0) gives +Inf. G(s) = (1.03e-13 s + 7.30e-14)/(s(s+1.33e-8)), so G(0) = Inf. The value equals B2/1.3258e-8, i.e. B1 was dropped as zero. The likely cause is the absolute coefficient floor in dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit or dcGainByStructuralEntries for tiny B (response.go). The branch gives the same result as base 2e4a07d. The sweep found 13 more TF.StateSpace realizations with a trailing-zero den (exact pole at s=0) where DCGain returns 0 and FR(0) returns +Inf.

[w12 #17 freq/review1] DCGain returns a finite value with the wrong sign and magnitude when the transfer limit is reached with a computed pole near DC. Repro (continuous companion): A row0 = -[6.325495602920146 12.427798551146598 7.785922515524618 2.9590313755032033e-05 2.830045401741772e-11 5.223977207934464e-19], subdiagonal ones, B=e1, C=[-0.1661821972150368 0.6204228877798674 1.5965704467083484 -0.2679049847206111 -0.17326373644234616 -0.9184631132625503], D=0.18013697908513038. The A solve fails (cond 1.4e21) and poleSpacing near=true (pole -1.88e-8). DCGain returns +9.684e11. The exact big.Rat G(0) is -1.758e18, FreqResponse(0) is +Inf, and ddResponseInto gives the exact value. Correct answers would be Inf (pole at DC) or -1.76e18; 9.7e11 is neither. Files: response.go (dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit). Same result on base 2e4a07d.

[w12 #18 freq/review2] Pre-existing (identical on base and branch), DCGain wrong next to near-DC poles in MIMO state-space models: for 49 of 1400 sweep models DCGain is +/-Inf or off while FreqResponse(0) matches the exact oracle. Its DCGain is finite but has relative error 5e-5 against the exact value (789372732529716 vs 789410222466333), and FreqResponse(0) is +Inf in every entry. Files: response.go (DCGain explicit solve / dcGainByTransferFunctionLimit), frequency_pole.go. Oracle: exact rational solve of C(s0 I-A)^-1 B+D.

[w12 #41 dcgain/review1] DCGain finite for an exactly singular dense block with no 1x1 exact pole (pre-existing, same on base 2e4a07d and branch). Repro: NewFromSlices(3,2,2, A=[0.38629023905802873 3.851534645926291 -3.23782488498432; 0 4 -3; 4 1.6251019182011088 -4.625101918201109], B=[-0.5 0; -1.75 0; 0 0], C=[-1 -2.176206339653932 1; 0 -0.06848213510526557 0], D=[5.737696031494993 0; 0.75 0], dt=0.1). title: EDGE: descriptor norms: pow2 equilibration before kappa(E) test; singular E keeps error (decided)
body:
Found in wave 15 (fix/wave15). [w15 #28 norms/JA65GD] JA65GD step 2, singular E in H2Norm/HinfNorm/Norm (owner decision needed). The MathWorks norm (control/ref/dynamicsystem.norm.html) and hinfnorm (robust/ref/dynamicsystem.hinfnorm.html) pages say nothing about dss, improper or singular-E models, so the precondition for implementing it is not met. Repro: NewDescriptor(A=[-1 1;0.5 -2], B=[1;1], C=[1 0], D=0, E=diag(1,0)) gives H2Norm/HinfNorm -> ErrDescriptorUnsupported wrapping ErrDescriptorSingular. When decided: properExplicitForm / conversionStandardForm (descriptor.go) already reduce proper index-1 models exactly. A continuous improper model plausibly gives Inf for both norms. A discrete improper (non-causal) model has bounded gain on the unit circle, so 'improper means Inf' does not follow there; the owner must settle that case.

[w15 #29 norms/JA65GD] Owner review of the cond(E) limit for norms: normDescriptorCondLimit = 1/sqrt(eps) ≈ 6.7e7 (descriptor.go). A legitimately stiff diagonal E, e.g. diag(1, 1e-9), still returns ErrDescriptorUnsupported. Base also errored, so no regression; loosen it if the owner prefers.

[w15 #30 norms/review0] JA65GD step 2 (planned, not a bug): support singular or improper descriptor E in H2Norm/HinfNorm/Norm after checking the MathWorks hinfnorm/norm docs. Also consider equilibrating E before the kappa guard, so that badly scaled diagonal E like diag(1e-8,1) is accepted (descriptor.go normExplicitForm).

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-21; MathWorks norm/hinfnorm pages checked)
- Equilibration is not a policy question: do pow2 row/column scaling (E→LER, A→LAR, B→LB, C→CR) before the κ(E) test. It is an exact equivalence, so the transfer function is unchanged. Keep the κ(E) error afterwards.
- Singular/improper E: neither page says anything about improper or singular-E models; they only say H∞ = Inf for unstable systems and H2 = Inf when unstable or continuous with nonzero D. Parity is undefined, so keep the documented error for singular E.
- LOW priority: this is feature scope behind the correctness backlog.

title: EDGE: AbsorbIO: keep non-decomposable residual as shared internal delays (minimality improvement; AY2CYR closed)
body:
Found in wave 17 (fix/wave17). AY2CYR partial merged (58fbbe4 tie-break). Remaining duplication argued structural; MATLAB has no IO-only absorb target.

[w17 #69 edges] AY2CYR: decide between (a) closing as partial / won't-fix, since one copy of the internal delays per piece is structural and MATLAB has no IO-only absorb to match, and (b) a new task to keep the non-decomposable residual as shared internal delays with the decomposable input and output delays absorbed as states. For the test plant (b) gives n=4, q=4, against today's n=7, q=4. Both are AbsorbIO in delay_residual_split.go.

[w17 #73 edges] AY2CYR reproduced. With n=1, m=3, p=2, a non-decomposable SetDelay, OutputDelay set, and 2 internal LFT delays: continuous AbsorbDelay(AbsorbIO) gives q=4 (2 column pieces) and discrete gives q=6 (3 column pieces). The response still matches the original. In the general case this cannot be soundly fixed:
(1) The duplication is structural, not a copying bug. Each split piece is out_g * G * in_g. A diagonal output delay does not commute with a non-diagonal G, so every group needs its own copy of the states, and the internal-delay loop (B2/C2/D22, Tau) goes with each copy. Sharing Tau channels across pieces would give a wrong model.
(2) For discrete AbsorbIO, the existing per-group cost (n + sum of in/out delay samples) is exactly the realized state count, so the base already picks the split with the fewest states. Weighting internal delays in the cost only trades states for channels. I tried it: discrete repro went 27 states/6 channels -> 33/4, with neither dominating, so I reverted it.
(3) MATLAB parity sets no achievable target. MATLAB ss has no IODelay matrix: a non-decomposable IODelay already becomes InternalDelay at construction, so "MATLAB keeps the original internal delays" describes a different model. It is not something this absorption path can match.
Delivered the one strictly better change (commit 58fbbe4, branch fix/edges-wave17, delay_residual_split.go newResidualDelaySplit). When row and column costs tie and the model has internal delays, pick the split with fewer pieces. Same state count, fewer duplicated internal-delay channels. q=0 behaviour is unchanged. Example: Delay [[3,1,0],[1,0,0]], dt=1, n=1, internal Tau [3,2]. AbsorbIO goes from 7 states/6 internal delays to 7/4. PullDelaysToLFT goes from 3 states/9 delays to 2/7. The original repro (no tie) is unchanged. A model with redundant internal delays is still correct; it is just not minimal.

[w17 #74 edges] QFAIOB is fixed (commit 91bca71 on fix/edges-wave17). AY2CYR reproduces but I left it alone: it needs a coordinator decision.

QFAIOB: I reproduced the bug. With A at scale 1e298 or 1e-300, 5 of the 6 points just off a real pole (all but λ≈-6.7e297) gave EvalFr = NaN with a nil error, while ddResponseInto had the right finite value. The fix is in /Users/josephj/workspace/controlsys/.claude/worktrees/wf_b27620d1-19f-28/frequency_hessenberg.go. A new helper, finiteResponse(dst), now runs at the end of both balancedDense.evalInto and hessenbergSweep.evalInto. If any output entry is NaN or Inf it returns errSingularPencil, which is not errNonFinitePencil, so evalWithPoleLimitGated goes on to the ddResponseInto / pole-limit fallback. All 6 repro points now match ddResponseInto. That includes the reviewer's case (b) at sc=1e-300, where base gave a wrong -2.0.

New test: TestEvalFrExtremeScaleNearPole in frequency_graded_test.go. The oracle is exact scale invariance: scaling A and B by a power of two (2^990 and 2^-996), and s by the same factor, leaves the response unchanged, so the unit-scale model gives the reference value. It checks EvalFr and both solvers through evalWithPoleLimit at s=λ(1-1e-10) for each real eigenvalue, with relative tolerance 1e-5. With the source change removed the test fails with NaN on 15 checks.

Benchmarks (benchcmp, base 7c14e32 against the working tree): +2.4% geomean, worst +5.8% (FreqResponseWithDelay), no extra allocations. Nothing near a 2x slowdown.

AY2CYR (not fixed, coordinator decision needed): it reproduces as described, q=4 against the reviewer's target of 2. I think the duplication is structural. The response is y = Σ_g Dout_g·H12·K·H21·Din_g·u_g, where K = Δ(I−H22Δ)⁻¹ is the internal-delay loop. The output delays Dout_g differ from piece to piece, and a single shared K loses which piece its output belongs to. So any realization that turns IO delays into states needs one copy of K per piece. The "MATLAB 2" target is also not something MATLAB does: MATLAB stores a non-decomposable ioDelay on an ss model as internal delays, and its absorbDelay on a discrete model absorbs every delay, internal ones included. There is no IO-only absorb mode to match.

For this test plant (total delay [[4,2,1],[1,0,0]], dt=1), the reviewer's alternative works out like this. The best split is input delay [1,0,0] plus output delay [1,0], leaving 2 residual entries ([2,1,0] on output 1). Absorbing the input and output delays as shifts and keepin


## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-22)
Close AY2CYR as done. The duplication is non-minimality by construction: the delay loop must travel with each non-commuting piece, the response matches, and MATLAB has no IO-only absorb. Option (b), shared internal delays, is filed as an EDGE improvement.

title: CORE: Pidtune PD-only ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable on unstable plants where PDF/TunePID succeed
body:
Found in wave 16 (fix/wave16). Likely PD-only raise/placement defect in pidtune.go. #14 (P on 1/(s^2+4s-5), max PM ~41.8 deg) lower confidence: check vs MATLAB pidtune, may be correct behaviour.

[w16 #12 pidtune/X57GVC] Pidtune PD unattainable where PDF/PID/PIDF succeed on unstable plants: Pidtune(1/(s(s-1)) i.e. TransferFunc num {1} den {1,-1,0} continuous, PidtunePD, 0, nil) and Pidtune(1/(s^2-0.5s+1), PidtunePD, 0, nil) return ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable. TunePID with this fix gives a PD at 2.22 rad/s (Kp~0.83, Kd~2.41) on the first plant and at 1.87 rad/s on the second; Routh confirms both stable and direct L(jwc) gives margin >= 57 deg. Pidtune's PDF on the same plants succeeds. Files: pidtune.go (PD placement, raised path). Likely a defect in Pidtune's PD-only raise or placement.

[w16 #13 pidtune/X57GVC] Pidtune PD unattainable on discrete 1/(z^2-2.1z+1.1), Dt 0.1, while TunePID gives a PD at 7.19 rad/s ('lowered' warning, already so on base). Files: pidtune.go. Should be checked against MATLAB.

[w16 #14 pidtune/X57GVC] Lower confidence: Pidtune P on 1/(s^2+4s-5) is unattainable although any K>5 stabilises it. The most phase margin a P can reach there is about 41.8 deg, so this may be Pidtune's correct '60 deg unreachable' behaviour rather than a defect; the coordinator should judge it against MATLAB pidtune. Files: pidtune.go.



Wave 17 reports:

[w17 #25] Owner decision, not a bug fix: 'PD' means three different filters across the API. Pidtune PD is filtered at Td/10. Pidtune PDF uses Tf = 0.1/wc (lighter). TunePID PD uses Tf = 0 (ideal). MATLAB pidtune 'PD' is believed to return an ideal PD (Tf = 0), with 'PDF' carrying the filter; this was not checked against the MATLAB doc page. If it holds, then per MATLAB parity Pidtune PD should be ideal, which would make the AMWRJU plants attainable. Repro: Pidtune(1/(s(s-1)), PD, 0, nil) and Pidtune(1/(s^2-0.5s+1), PD, 0, nil) return unattainable, while TunePID gives Tf=0 PDs with PM 57 deg. Evidence: the filtered lead is capped at asin(10/12) = 56.44 deg; see TestPidtuneFilteredPDUnattainable. Files: pidtune.go computePD/placedPD (the doc line 'Callers requesting an ideal PD must explicitly set Tf=0'). Changing it would reshape every existing PD test, so it needs an owner call.

[w17 #35] Owner decision AMWRJU: Pidtune PD family. (1) Always ideal (MATLAB parity): accept PID.System errors on Tf=0, |S|=Inf on delayed and biproper plants, and value->error in LevelCappedGainSource and AutoPDZeroDCMargin. (2) Hybrid: ideal first, then the Td/10 pipeline as fallback. This doubles the PD pipeline and still leaves PID.System erroring. (3) Status quo: the AMWRJU goal stays unmet. Evidence is the experiment's 15 failing tests; files are pidtune.go computePD/placedPD/pipeline and pidtune_wave17_test.go.

[w17 #49] AMWRJU reproduced on fix/pidtune-wave17: all 4 cases return ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable. This is correct fail-closed behaviour for Pidtune's controller families, not a defect in the PD raise/placement path, so there is no sound fix within the current PD definition. No production code changed.

Root cause: Pidtune's PD is always Td/10-filtered, C = Kp(1+1.1Td s)/(1+0.1Td s), a lead of ratio 11 whose phase never exceeds asin(10/12) = 56.44 deg. TunePID's PD is ideal (its outputs show Tf:0 with PM 57.0 deg on each plant). That is a different controller family, not a better search.

Evidence comes from an independent oracle. It grids K (both signs) and Td, keeps only loops whose closed-loop roots (companion-matrix eigenvalues) are stable, and takes the smallest margin over all gain crossovers. Best margins it finds:
- 1/(s(s-1)), PD: 55.45 deg. Analytically PM = atan(w) + phiC - 90, so it is bounded by 56.44.
- 1/(s^2-0.5s+1), PD: 55.95 deg.
- Discrete 1/((z-1)(z-1.1)), Dt 0.1, PD: 30.44 deg.
- 1/(s^2+4s-5), P: 41.81 deg, equal to atan(sqrt5) - atan(sqrt5/5). This confirms #14 is correct behaviour.

All four are below the 58.5 bar, so failing closed is required (5UUEZD). Pidtune's PDF (Tf = 0.1/wc) is oracle-robust on the two continuous plants.

Added the persistent test TestPidtuneFilteredPDUnattainable in /Users/josephj/workspace/controlsys/.claude/worktrees/wf_b27620d1-19f-12/pidtune_wave17_test.go. It first checks the oracle itself: P on 1/(s-1) and PD on 1/(s(s+1)) must reach above 58.5. title: DECISION: TunePIDFRD default crossover above RHP zero visible in sampled phase (2FQ6DJ #18b)
body:
Found in wave 17 (fix/wave17). 2FQ6DJ follow-up: design near-critical with |S|~4e3 and warning.

[w17 #24 pidtune] #18b only partly fixed: no PDF design within |S|<=4 exists at the default FRD crossover (0.32 rad/s, above the plant's right-half-plane zero at 0.0225), so the design comes back with true |S| of about 4e3 and a warning. The DC sign is now checked against the size of the gap between the lowest sample and DC, but the design is still near-critical. Worth deciding whether the default FRD crossover should account for a right-half-plane zero visible in the sampled phase.


## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-22)
No RHP-zero heuristic. The FRD default crossover should take the Pidtune auto path: gate, back off, then search upward. Above the RHP zero the gate fails, so the design lands below it. Base designs with |S|~4e3 are not robust, so flips are allowed. Fold into the PN7T63 redo.

Wave 17 reports:

[w17 #66] Regression from PAOH7X/LP755Y: the breakaway at a multiple pole at the origin is lost for pure integrator chains (k/s^2) when the realization is not triangular. cutoffFloors only treats a pole set as unscaled when every pole is exactly 0. When rounding splits the double pole at 0 (to ±1.6e-16i or ±3.5e-9), the floor becomes that split, so both the nearRealCount repeat window and the cluster test shrink to about 1e-22 and miss it. The real-axis parity rule then decides by chance, depending on which way the split goes and on the gain sign. Base used an absolute 1e-4 window and gave [0], which is correct and robust at unit scale. The branch's own computeBreakaway doc says a net multiple pole is a breakaway, and the exact oracle agrees: q = -N·D' = -2k·s, so s=0 is a double pole with K=0. The same cause makes rotated 1/s^3 return [] (want [0]); base was also wrong there (spurious -8.4e7 only), so that one is not a regression. title: Pidtune 100-200ms on zero-DC continuous-delay plants when back-off fails everywhere (owner decision)
body:
Found in wave 10 (PR pending, branch fix/wave10).

BIAA3G leftover: on stable zero-DC plants with a continuous delay where the back-off fails everywhere, Pidtune still costs about 100 to 200 ms per call (120 gate checks, dominated by golden-section |S| refinement on delay ripple in pidTuningSensitivityPeak and tailPeak), against about 1 ms before #345, which did not back off on these plants. Examples: P -0.71 s/(s^2+7.44 s+36.6) tau 0.664; PD (-0.464 s^2-0.366 s)/(s^3+11.5 s^2+43.6 s+54.3) tau 0.486. Closing the gap needs a sound early stop for the back-off (no candidate found) or a cheaper |S| refinement rule; that is an owner decision.

title: CORE: Care/Dare icare-style Accuracy report (0 certified / 1 poor X returned) to recover fail-closed flips (decided)
body:
Found in wave 17 (fix/wave17). Riccati step 1 landed as dd-residual Newton step certificate (pencil X step<=1e-8, iterate<=1e-10), deviating from decided OIBDKX dd backward-error gate (measured unsound). Owner: confirm deviation; decide whether to recover cheap-control/weak-actuation values now ErrNoStabilizing (options: structured forward-error/condition estimate, defect-correction Riccati solve, or accept Schur X as MATLAB icare). Extended-precision Kleinman step ruled out.

[w17 #1 riccati] Owner decision needed, replacing the OIBDKX decision: accepting Care/Dare X by double-double residual is unsound. Wrong X were seen with residuals at or below the rounded exact solution's: weakBStall 0.46x at error 3.4e-6 (320-bit), unstableK (Dare) 1.1e-16 at error 1e-5. Accurate Schur X were seen with residuals up to 0.17 (cheap590, error 4.4e-11; ch360 2.3e-5 at 8.6e-12). Options still open: (a) a structured forward-error or condition estimate, (b) accept the Schur X as MATLAB icare does and treat a large pencil residual only as grounds to reject. Option (c), an extended-precision Lyapunov or Newton step, is ruled out: an exact 320-bit Kleinman step from ch360's Schur X (error 8.6e-12) lands at 6.7e-7.

[w17 #9 riccati] Owner decision needed: the fail-closed cost of step (1). Care with cheap control and weak actuation now returns ErrNoStabilizing where base returned an X within 1e-8. Counts: 23/26 of 10000 solves without E (arm64/amd64), and 3/7 and 0/1 of 8000 with E. Only 7 of 26 arm64 flips are robust on base under 1-ulp perturbations. Examples: e1768 Care+E NoScaling (base 2.1e-12, robust per review), ch360 default (base 8.6e-12), w16 #4 default (base 2.44e-9). Cause: Newton has no quadratic region there. The exact 320-bit Kleinman step from the 8.6e-12 ch360 X is 8e-7, and the dd backward residual is measured unusable. A possible cure is a properly scaled defect-correction Riccati solve (A_KᵀF + FA_K − FGF + Ric_dd(X) = 0) as an error estimate. Files: riccati.go (verifyRiccati, newtonCost).

[w17 #10 riccati] Deviation from the OIBDKX decision: acceptance uses the dd-residual forward Newton step (pencil X at 1e-8 or less, iterate at 1e-10 or less), not a dd backward-error threshold. The measurement shows no backward-error threshold exists, and the ordering is inverted: rounded cheap-control oracle X at 1e-6 vs a 5.4e-7-wrong w15 #16 X at 3.4e-11 under the plain scale; a 8.6e-12-accurate ch360 X at 6.7e-17 vs a 9.7e-7-wrong w15 #17 iterate at 8.1e-18 under the gain-form scale. The coordinator should confirm. Commit c93f04e.

[w17 #18 riccati] I rebuilt branch fix/riccati-wave17 so the three steps land in the required order. The branch keeps 2998bb4 (the oracle test). The old commits 9a772cc and 3dcef47 are replaced (3dcef47 is cherry-picked as e78567c). Nothing is pushed; HEAD is detached at 1d7d8c9. Each step is its own commit group:
(1) c93f04e. U2UHH5/F2ZLBA/OIBDKX, non-E Care and Dare.
(2) fdb33c4. MW6KWB/7OUOQO, Care and Dare with E.
(3) e78567c + 1d7d8c9. XACVXD.

Step (1) decision. I re-measured the decided dd backward-error gate. No threshold works, and the ordering is inverted:
- With the plain relative residual, the correctly rounded cheap-control X sits at 1e-6..2e-6. The w15 #16 X, wrong by 5.4e-7, sits at 3.4e-11.
- With a gain-form rounding scale, the ch360 X with error 8.6e-12 sits at 6.7e-17. A w15 #17 iterate wrong by 9.7e-7 sits at 8.1e-18.

So I failed closed, using a forward certificate. **This deviates from the decided certificate; the coordinator should confirm it.** How it works:
- The Newton step is computed from the double-double residual (riccatiResidual from 861c1bb).
- The pencil X is kept only if its first step is 1e-8 or less. Across about 60 records, the exact 320-bit step from a pencil X never understated the error by more than 3x.
- A Newton iterate is kept only at a step of 1e-10 or less. Iterates can hide error: one had a step of 3e-9 with an error of 2.4e-7.
- Removed: the Care stall exit, the Dare stall exit (including the single-step one), the Lyapunov-singular iterate exit, and the `exact` backward-error accept. That last one kept the noiseFloor X at 4.9e-7 on amd64.

Step (2) uses the same certificate in generalized form: F = E⁻¹A_K, Y = EᵀΔE, the residual has the E terms, and careGain uses BᵀXE. It does not use 9a772cc's float64 Newton gate at 1e-8. descriptorCare and rescued are removed, and E now goes through pencilRiccati (candidates and lastResort).

Step (3) wires the reciprocal-pencil retry into the Riccati pencil (stableDeflatingQZ, called by generalizedStableSubspace) and into properExplicitForm (orderedQZ and qzSylvester). A retry is kept only when its eigenvalues match the first run one to one; otherwise it still returns ErrSchurFailed.

Review findings:
- #4 (strict order): fixed by the rebuild.
- #3 (step 1 missing): landed as above. ch360 NoScaling, which returned a silent 2.7e-7 X, is now an error. Dare w15 #16, w15 #17 and fastSampled now converge to about 1e-13.
- #2 (race failure): fixed. TestDescriptorRiccatiVerified now returns every X

## Decision (advisor, 2026-10-22)
The c93f04e certificate stays as the interim rule. It accepts X when the double-double Newton step is ≤1e-8 for a pencil X or ≤1e-10 for an iterate. Across the corpus it never certified a wrong X.
- The wave 17 PR merges it, accepting 26 value→error flips in 10,000 solves, 7 of them robust on base (ch360 8.6e-12, e1768 2.1e-12, w16#4 2.4e-9). The alternative left two classes of silently wrong X on main.
- Recovery follows icare parity. Add an additive Accuracy/Report field to the Riccati result:
  - 0: accurate (Newton-certified).
  - 1: poor (stabilizing pencil X, not certified).
  - 2: non-finite.
  - 3: no stabilizing solution.
  X is returned for 0 and 1; 2, 3 and pencil failure are errors.
- The MathWorks icare page lists X=[] only for Report 3 and 4, which implies X is returned at Report 1.
- weakBStall is the guard: it must report 1, never 0.
- Optional: test whether e²‖G‖‖L_K⁻¹‖ at ch360 reproduces the ~8e-7 step. If it does, invert it into an error estimate.

title: EDGE: TunePIDFRD Nyquist count certifies unstable loops: no DC anchor, loose top-end rules
body:
Found in wave 16 (fix/wave16). Gaps in PHCKA5 pidTuningFRDNyquistCount / pidTuningFRDDCGain end anchors; pre-existing unstable gains, result carries finite-coverage warning.

[w16 #15 pidtune/PHCKA5] TunePIDFRD still returns unstable loops on data with no flat DC end (pidTuningFRDDCGain returns 0, so neither the DC test nor the Nyquist count applies), although MATLAB's NumUnstablePoles=0 default applies to any frd. Repro: frd = pidExactFRD(num [-1.6397335053538995 0.022678154196576948], den [1 0.05699814057448621 0.0010336161545953615 5.660971928156559e-06], 1e-3, 1e3, 100); TunePIDFRD(PI, PhaseMargin 45) gives Kp -0.4355, Ki 0.4190, and pidClosedLoopMaxRe is +0.608. The lowest sample is about 3862-1004j, which is not flat. Fixing it needs a low-end anchor, for example the low-frequency asymptote's order and phase. Files: pid_tuning_frd.go (pidTuningFRDDCGain, pidTuningFRDNyquistCount).

[w16 #20 pidtune/review1] PHCKA5 top-end rules in pidTuningFRDNyquistCount (pid_tuning_frd.go) can certify unstable loops when the data stop before the loop rolls off. This is new code, but no regression: base also returned unstable gains in every such case. (a) The 'default:' arm sets end = 1 + Re L(top) for any continuous L within 30° of the real axis with |L| >= 1. It does not check c.Tf == 0 or the plant's relative degree. For a filtered derivative (or no D) on a strictly proper plant, L -> 0 past the band, so the true end is +1 and a ±π turn is missed. Repro: num {2.166140865041497, 16.891340677621397, 6.110303450674674, 0.4018892635929858}, den {1, 23.952741735010143, 226.10414419796365, 543.5529399666149, 325.67512854605485}; frd = pidExactFRD(num, den, 1e-2, 10, 100); TunePIDFRD(PIDF, PIDTuningOptions{}). It returns Kp -113.26, Ki -83.10, Kd -545.73, Tf 0.1918, and pidTuningFRDNyquistCount gives (true, true) with dcGain 0.001232. |L(10)| is 318 at -158.9°. A dense independent unwrap of 1+L over 1e-7..1e6 gives Δ = -0.498π against +0.5π for stable, so Z = 1, and the exact Routh test says unstable. Suggested fix: when Tf != 0 or Kd == 0, treat |L(top)| >= 1 as unknown (reject). (b) The 'case |L| < 1' arm takes the loop as rolled off without the falling check the |L| >= 1 arm makes. On discrete data that stop at 0.3-0.7 of Nyquist, |L| rises above 1 again past the band. Repros (G sampled at n log points on [1e-3/dt, frac·π/dt], exact Schur-Cohn oracle): dt 1, lag 1, num {1.4351105419474985}, den {1, 0.3657232065834215}, frac 0.7, n 500, PID with PM 45 (FE/FE) -> Kp -0.55978, Ki 0.035465, Kd 0, unstable; |L(top)| 0.988, max |L| past top 1.31. Another: dt 0.05, lag 0, num {0.5285655144705834}, den {1, 0.27082365510092343, 0.13777847481081767}, frac 0.3, n 50, PI with PM 45 (IFormula Trapezoidal) -> Kp -1.6825, Ki 1.2686, unstable. A continuous truncated-band sweep (hi 1-10 rad/s, n=300) gave 7 of 293 successes certified but unstable. The result always carries the finite-coverage warning, and these cases are outside the task's listed repros.



Wave 17 reports:

[w17 #26] TunePIDFRD discrete |L|>=1 'falling, <2' top-end arm certifies unstable loops on data that stop short of Nyquist. pidTuningFRDNyquistCount in pid_tuning_frd.go, case '!nearReal || c.Dt > 0', ends 1+L at 1 when |L(top)| is in [1,2) and falling, but a discrete L ends at the real L(z=-1) and can stay above 1. Repro: dt=1, num [1.1272406328814324], den [1 1.1684544028120818 1.0260321132310026 0.29572027153985536 -0.0373213055162959], sampled at 100 log points on [0.038707392544896815, 0.7π]. TunePIDFRD(PI, PhaseMargin 45, IFormula ForwardEuler, DFormula BackwardEuler) gives Kp 0.7105312658025903, Ki 0.8655482384549156. |L(top)| is 1.289 at -175° (1.699 at the sample before), max |L| past the data is 1.289, and exact Schur-Cohn says unstable. Present on base too: 12 of the 27 remaining unstable results in the stable-plant sweep and about 15 of the 25 in the integrating sweep. The arm is pinned by TestTunePIDFRDNyquistKeepsFallingTop (|L| about 1.005 at 0.3π), so this needs an owner decision, for example a |L(top)| < 1.05 cap.

[w17 #27] pidTuningFRDDCGain takes an integrator hidden behind a zero just below the band for a DC end, so the count certifies unstable loops. Pre-existing; the strict path is affected too. Repro: continuous num [-0.24436543075354913 0.009229922316894113], den [1 4.734640851796328 16.2011199053105 0] (integrator, unstable zero at 0.0378), 100 log points on [0.04353021199383071, 1.4803666719297164]. TunePIDFRDF... more precisely TunePIDFRD(PIDF, PhaseMargin 45) gives Kp 59.347708325267654, Ki -18.199284260310943, Kd -125.57441253934684, Tf 1.7654754475491596. dcGain is taken as -0.01525; the true G at 0.0044 rad/s is -0.0152-0.131j. pidClosedLoopMaxRe is +0.0332. Same class: 9 of the 25 remaining unstable results in the integrating sweep. A possible tightening is a Bode gain-phase consistency check on the DC path, but that would reject minimum-phase-inconsistent DC ends such as the PN7T63 case A plant.

[w17 #28] |L(top)| < 1 that is flat or barely falling at the top sample still ends the count at 1, though |L| rises past the band. Not knowable from the data; only stricter slope rules fix it, at high cost (a log-slope <= -0.5 rule lost 122 more stable designs while removing only 8 unstable ones). Repro: continuous num [-0.4156058126006063 -0.7551548371911957], den [1 114.20727027161044 4604.154939900912], 300 log points on [0.01042111217302736, 1.1785809567972114]. TunePIDFRD(PIDF, defaults) gives Kp 3347.8068011369137, Ki -672.1489827804135, Kd -8158.033287328667, Tf 2.9586115757568936. |L(top)| is 0.15948 (0.15996 at the sample before), max |L| past the band is 2.15, and maxRe is +81.5. Pre-existing on base.

[w17 #29] Discrete near-Nyquist arm: when nyquist && !nearReal && |L(top)| < 1, the end is accepted with no rise check, as on base. Repro: dt=1, num [-0.188025172614477], den [1 -2.0543616351871403 1.3452532933647021 -0.29089165817756185 0] (integrating), 50 log points on [0.007650792583208919, 0.95π]. TunePIDFRD(PIDF, PhaseMargin 45, IFormula BackwardEuler, DFormula ForwardEuler) gives Kp -0.18919360498190374, Ki -0.015523854772838689, Kd -0.5999257320736973, Tf 0.5100004458961601. |L| rises from 0.206 to 0.600 over the last sample step at -88.8°, max |L| to Nyquist is 2.40, and exact Schur-Cohn says unstable. The filter pole is near z=-1 because Tf is about Dt/2.

[w17 #30] UX, not fixed: on data with no anchor, TunePIDFRD now searches its full evaluation budget and returns a generic ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable. It could fail fast right after pidTuningFRDPlant when p.nyquistCount && p.dcGain == 0 && !p.lowAnchor, returning a *PIDTuningError whose evidence warning says to extend the data toward DC or set UnstablePoles. That would keep errors.Is behavior unchanged. Only the exported doc of TunePIDFRD is updated so far.

[w17 #36] Owner confirmation PN7T63 residual: in my 1000-case proxy sweep, 15 cases are robust on base and error on f21b228. 11 are low-truncated bands starting near a lightly damped resonance. 4 are top-truncated bands with |L| >= 1 at the top sample. All are rejected by fail-closed because the data don't fix that end.

[w17 #37] Minor followup, no false certification: pidTuningDCAdmissible (pid_tuning.go:851-871) still ends an ideal derivative at 1+Re L(top) when |L| >= 1 and near-real. It can only reject, but it rejects spuriously where sign(1+Re L(top)) differs from sign(1+Kd*lim sG). It should take p.markov, which needs plumbing.

[w17 #38] Discrete FRD: falling |L|<1 at the top sample, short of Nyquist, is still accepted when |L| rises past 1 before z=-1. Cause: pidTuningFRDTopBounded extrapolates |G| at its log slope, but a discrete |G| flattens toward Nyquist, so it underestimates |G| there when a derivative filter pole near -1 or a plant pole near -1 lifts |L|. This exists in base, f21b228 and 8cbb362. Repro (seeded sweep case 2867): num [-1.3448981227532175], den [1 -1.5811862552962634 0.8405266355392914 -0.2593403802430281], dt 0.1, pidExactFRD-style log grid of 422 points on [0.5184154210153508, 17.34960121464623] filled with G(e^{jωdt}). Call TunePIDFRD(PIDF, PIDTuningOptions{PhaseMargin: 60, IFormula: BackwardEuler, DFormula: ForwardEuler}). It returns Kp -0.13939, Ki -0.030937, Kd -0.015729, Tf 0.054975. The count gives (true, true) but exact Schur-Cohn says unstable. |L(top)| is 0.335 and falling, but the true max |L| above the band is 1.21; the forward-Euler derivative pole is at 1-dt/Tf = -0.82. Similar: cases 359 and 2975 (an ideal forward-Euler D with Kd 4.7, dt 1). File: pid_tuning_frd.go, pidTuningFRDTopBounded and the |L|<1 branch of pidTuningFRDNyquistCount. A possible fix is to extrapolate |G| symmetrically about Nyquist for discrete data.

[w17 #39] Continuous FRD, ideal derivative (Tf=0) on a biproper plant whose data stop below a far zero: pidTuningFRDMarkov sees jω·G as flat at the top and the asymptote rule ends 1+L at 1+Kd·lim sG. The true G(∞) is nonzero, so L→∞ and the closed loop has a large positive root. This exists in base and f21b228; my anchor change exposes it on more data. Repro (sweep case 1447): num [-0.9043089425627748 -1256.883521757146 -389.6467771092301], den [1 6.820830968278832 34.526396140064016], continuous, 271 log points on [1.3086639769123847, 147.87950751653452]. Call TunePIDFRD(PD, PIDTuningOptions{PhaseMargin: 30}). It returns Kp -0.000531, Kd 0.00076, Tf 0, with max closed-loop Re +141.8. The plant zero is at 1390 rad/s, about a decade above the top sample. Similar: case 1531 (zero at 612 rad/s, top sample 220 rad/s). Arguably the data cannot show this, but an ideal-D design that relies on lim sG from data stopping a decade below a possible zero may deserve an owner decision (for example, require Tf>0, or treat this end as unknown when the data do not reach well past the plant poles). File: pid_tuning_frd.go, pidTuningFRDMarkov and the asymptote branch of pidTuningFRDNyquistCount.

[w17 #44] TunePIDFRD can return a forward-Euler ideal-derivative controller (Tf 0, DFormula FE) on biproper discrete data. The count assumes L is proper (no pole at z = infinity), so it certifies unstable loops, and PID.System rejects the controller as noncausal (pre-existing, base-identical). Repro 1914: num [3.393044303813305, -0.27295347658179514, -3.3082691822417116, 0.16753894363629457], den [1, -1.6457107028224587, 0.3553134944360514, 0.29046578031903075], dt 0.1, 365 log points on [0.2162, 11.67], TunePIDFRD(PD, PhaseMargin 45, IFormula Trapezoidal). Result: Kp 0.012539, Kd -0.018759, count (true, true), closed loop |z| = 1.509. File: pid_tuning_frd.go (pidTuningFRDNyquistCount).

[w17 #45] TunePIDFRD discrete forward-Euler ideal derivative (Tf=0) on biproper data: the Nyquist count ignores L's pole at z=inf and certifies unstable loops. This predates the branch and gives the same result on base. Repro: discrete FRD dt=1, G = (1.1165872865935105 z^2 - 0.8967939326027657 z + 0.05725857765328797)/(z^2 - 1.099536361782705 z + 0.16610723397810698), 218 log points on [0.0013434142960855107, 3.0216239262734725], TunePIDFRD(PidtunePID, {}). It returns Kp 0.002589, Ki 0.018529, Kd -0.059611, Tf 0 with nil error; companion and Schur-Cohn put a closed-loop root at z = 15.8, and pidTuningFRDNyquistCount gives (true,true) with dcGain 4.16. Same class: sweep ids 2385 (PD, root 1.069), 2498 (PD, root 198), 2015 (PID, root 7.9), 2267 (PID, root -9.8), all biproper, DFormula ForwardEuler, Tf 0. Cause: Kd(z-1)/Ts is improper, so with D!=0 the loop has P=1 at infinity. Files: pid_tuning_frd.go pidTuningFRDNyquistCount. Fix idea: reject or count the infinite pole when Dt>0, Tf=0, DFormula=ForwardEuler, Kd!=0, unless the data show relative degree >= 1.

[w17 #50] Branch fix/pidtune-wave17, one commit f21b228 (not pushed, HEAD detached). Findings 1 and 2 fixed; finding 3 not landed and needs an owner decision.

Finding 1 (PN7T63 value->error, reproduced). Fail-closed is kept. The fix widens what the sampled Nyquist count can certify, in pid_tuning_frd.go:
(a) pidTuningFRDLowOrder now tries the order-0 test first for any |slope| < 1. The integer orders are tried only for |slope| > 0.75. This fixes #496, whose secant slope of -0.756 fell between orders.
(b) A new m==0 arm handles order-0 low ends with no integral action (P/PD/PDF). It calls pidTuningFRDFlatLoopStart, which accepts when either: Kp·G(low) is on the positive side and its phase plus asin(|Kd·d|/|Kp|) is under 90°; or |L| < 1 below the band, using |G(0)| <= |G(low)|/cos φ. An order-0 loop on an integrating or differentiating end cancels that end and stays unknown. The first version allowed this and the LowAnchorMatchesClosedLoopRoots tripwire caught real false certifications.
Reviewer cases #172 PD, #496 PI and #19 P now return base's designs (PM 63/63/90).
Proxy sweep (my own seeded 1000 cases in the reviewer's shape; I don't have the reviewer's seeds): 22 designs robust on base but erroring on head. 8 are recovered. 15 errors remain against base:
- 11 low-truncated bands starting at or just below a lightly damped resonance: slope and phase disagree, so the data don't fix the low end.
- 4 top-truncated bands where |L| >= 1 at the top sample and the data stop before roll-off. One of these, #671, head certified only through the faulty adjacent-flatness rule of finding 2. That is an intended trade, not a regression.
#664 goes from error back to base's stable design with a |S|-exceeds-4 warning (existing documented behaviour). No new unstable designs: the one unstable case (#293) is the same on base and head.

Finding 2 (reproduced: n=200/400 count was (true,true) on an unstable loop). The adjacent-sample 1% flatness rule is gone. A new plant-side anchor, pidTuningFRDMarkov, accepts continuous data only when |G| has slope within 0.1 of -1 over the top half decade and jω·G is within 30° of the real axis. It stores markov = lim sG and markovSpread = |Re change|. An ideal derivative then ends at 1 + Kd·markov, gated on its real part keeping sign against Re(1 + L(top)) - end and 2|Kd|·spread; otherwise the end is unknown. A continuous near-real end with |L| >= 1 and no anchor is unknown. pidTuningEdgeSensitivity now includes |S| at the Markov end, so near-flip de


Wave 17 reports:

[w17 #46] PN7T63 value->error: TunePIDFRD now returns ErrPIDTuningTargetUnattainable on cases where base 79a3737 returned a design that is oracle-stable and robust (|S|<=4, PM ok). Every one fails closed by the new count rules. Seeded sweep, seed 7, 2500 cases: 8 robust cases (plus 4 fragile ones with base |S|>4 or PM<58.5, not counted), out of about 400 FRD designs base returned. Sorted by cause: (a) low end cannot be anchored, dcGain=0 and lowAnchor=false: ids 391, 872, 1656, 2468. (b) a low order is anchored but the start case is unknown: id 960, lowOrder=1 on a plant with DC gain -5.6, |L(low)|>0.5. For 1284 the data cannot decide: the true |L(z=-1)| is 1.19, past the data, so it may be inherent fail-closed and an owner call.
Oracle: exact big.Rat Routh/Schur-Cohn on den*Cd+num*Cn, plus dense |S| and PM sweeps. Base controllers checked with the branch's pidTuningFRDNyquistCount give (true,false), i.e. not certified. title: Pidtune ~6-8x slower on simple auto calls since AUOTFB first-design gate (owner decision on gate grid)
body:
Found in wave 10 (PR pending, branch fix/wave10).

Perf (CR7GLM, caused by AUOTFB): newPidtuneGate now runs on every automatic Pidtune call. It evaluates the plant about 3000 times (sens grid about 230 points/decade, cross grid 100/decade, no shared points, band floor*1e-3 to wc*1e3). Result: about 8x slower on BenchmarkPidtune_PI/PID/PIDF (93us to 760us, 25KB to 388KB/op) and +66% on the continuous-delay sweep. Options: share or interpolate the sens and cross plant samples, cheaper pole-residue evaluation of the SISO plant on the grids, or lazy top-down |S| scanning. Files: pidtune.go (newPidtuneGate, pidtuneGate.sensitivityOver, crossExcess). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune.

Pidtune slowdown on simple plants from 027664e (AUOTFB first-design gate). Repro: go run ./scripts/benchcmp -base 8cfed86 -candidate 027664e -bench Pidtune. Evidence, 8cfed86 to HEAD: Pidtune_PI 80 us to 711 us (+787%), PID +836%, PIDF +751%, PidtuneFastSampled/O2 42 us to 797 us (+1795%), O5 +429%, Delayed/PI +185%, Delayed/PD 1.0 ms to 15 ms (+1358%), Delayed/PIDF +142%; B/op 25 KB to 388 KB, allocs/op +42% to +60% (Delayed/PD +2190%, of which my commits recover 8.6%). The 027664e-vs-HEAD benchcmp shows my commits leave time unchanged, so this all comes from 027664e. Cause: every automatic first design now builds newPidtuneGate, which samples about 9+ decades ([floor*1e-3, wc*1e3]) even when the design then passes. Files: pidtune.go (Pidtune, run.design(wc, sign, auto), newPidtuneGate). Narrowing the band or building the gate lazily could change gate verdicts, so this is an owner decision; not fixed.

Pidtune small automatic calls still cost about 470us vs 77us on 8cfed86 (Pidtune_PI/PID/PIDF, FastSampled ~2.6x). Cause: AUOTFB gates every auto first design on the full back-off gate grid, [floor*1e-3, wc*1e3] at 1% steps (about 2100 plant solves, pidtune.go newPidtuneGate). Lowering it means building the first design's grid lazily or narrowing it, which changes verdicts on some plants; that needs an owner decision.

Perf: BenchmarkPidtune_Delayed/PD (0.3s-1/(s+1)^4, input delay 5, PD, wc=0) is 1.1-1.2ms on base and about 18-28ms now. The gated first design (|S| 7.6) fails, all 60 back-off steps run gate checks and fail, then the ungated first design is returned as the fallback. A faster failing gate path or an earlier stop (e.g. when |S| rises steadily as wc drops) would recover this. File: pidtune.go (Pidtune back-off loop).

Perf (minor, existing pattern): on the reflected-delay path, r.screened(wc) and checkPidtuneStability each call screen.at(wc, family), which builds pidTuningDelayStability state twice per step that reaches Nyquist. The same double call happens on the non-delay gated path (r.gated(pid, wc, r.screened(wc))). Files: pidtune.go (pidtuneRun.check), pid_tuning.go (pidStabilityScreen.at).

BenchmarkPidtune_BackoffFail/GateP is +7% (3.52 to 3.77 ms) after the crossover scan moved to the finer |S| grid (16add00). Repro: benchcmp -base b0e01b5 -candidate 9b2e8d4 -bench ^BenchmarkPidtune. Most of it is bisection and golden-section refinement calls into the memoized p.at during back-off steps that fail anyway.

title: CORE: SS->TF fast-mode rel-degree-5 class keeps untrimmed num -> spurious huge ZPK zeros
body:
Found in wave 17 (fix/wave17). 4INCJC remainder: markovTrim.trim never offers MATLAB's trim; needs sensitivity-aware per-point tolerance.

[w17 #20 tf] MATLAB degree parity for the fast-mode dense relative-degree-5 class (e.g. the wave-16 review repro, poles -75840 -3 -3.51+-4.74i -9.88 -28.5, zero +0.429) is still open. Head keeps the base untrimmed numerator, so ZPKModel has spurious huge zeros; MATLAB would give num [4.878, -2.094]. markov.trim never offers that candidate: it offers only max/min(lead, r-off). At noise-dominated check points the correct trim has eT ~ 1, so the 2*eF rule cannot accept it. A fix needs a sensitivity-aware per-point tolerance, e.g. the first-order bound eps*(|y|^T|A||x| + |y|^T|B| + |C||x|) with x=(sI-A)^-1 B and y=(sI-A)^-T C^T, plus offering every intermediate trim. Files: transfer.go (markovTrim.trim, tfCheck.trimOK).

title: EDGE: FRDFeedback m>p absolute pivot tol: false ErrAlgebraicLoop at ||KG||>1e15
body:
Found in wave 13 (fix/wave13).

[w13 #56 fuzz/MOI6LA] [EDGE] FRDFeedback with more plant inputs than outputs solves the m x m system I - sign*K*G with an absolute pivot tolerance (cSolveInPlace). It loses accuracy at a relative error of about eps*||KG|| and returns a false ErrAlgebraicLoop once ||KG|| exceeds about 1e15, although (I+GK)^-1 G is well-conditioned. Repro: G = [[3c+ci, -2c+0.5ci]] (1x2), K = [[0.3],[0.2]], sign = -1. At c=1e14 the relative error is 4e-3; at c=1e15 it is 20%; at c>=1e16 it returns ErrAlgebraicLoop. The exact answer is G/(1+GK), about 4.63-1.71i. Files: frd.go FRDFeedback, frequency.go cSolveInPlace. Fix: solve the smaller p x p I - sign*G*K when p < m, or use a relative pivot test.
